connections.observation: ὄψον appears first as something absent from necessities, then as a simple addition, then as conventional luxury, and finally in a catalogue where necessities are no longer the criterion (οὐκέτι τἀναγκαῖα θετέον). The same word traverses the boundary from absent to necessary to unnecessary.

Glaucon calls the simple city a city of pigs (ὑῶν πόλιν); swineherds (συβωτῶν) appear only when forms of δέω/προσδέω accumulate densely, marking needs generated by luxury. Pigs absent from the city of pigs return as a need in the expanded city.

Health language (ὑγιείας, ὑγιής, ὑγιεινή) characterizes the first city and its sufficiency (ἱκανή), while the second is inflamed (φλεγμαίνουσαν) and insufficient (οὐκέτι ἱκανή). The shift from health to fever coincides with the shift from sufficiency to insufficiency.

The simple city lives in peace (ἐν εἰρήνῃ); the section ends with war's genesis (πολέμου γένεσιν) after transgressing the boundary of necessities (ὑπερβάντες τὸν τῶν ἀναγκαίων ὅρον) requires cutting off neighbors' land (ἀποτμητέον). Peace and a boundary become war and transgression.

τραγήματα, κλῖναι, and τράπεζαι appear first in Glaucon's demand, then return in Socrates' catalogue alongside perfumes, incense, courtesans, gold, and ivory (s012). Items Glaucon names as conventional necessities reappear among luxury's proliferations.

τὸ ἀναγκαῖον recurs three times as a criterion, then as something no longer operative (οὐκέτι τοῦ ἀναγκαίου ἕνεκά), and finally as a limit/boundary (τὸν τῶν ἀναγκαίων ὅρον) that is overstepped (ὑπερβάντες). Necessity shifts from criterion to transgressed boundary.

Forms of δέω/προσδέω concentrate at 373c, where two catalogues (hunters, imitators, poets, rhapsodes, actors, dancers; then tutors, wet-nurses, beauticians, barbers, cooks, butchers) accumulate. The multiplication of needs generates the multiplication of occupational types.

The simple city hands down the same life to offspring (ἄλλον τοιοῦτον βίον τοῖς ἐκγόνοις παραδώσουσιν); the luxurious expansion produces the genesis of war (πολέμου γένεσιν ηὑρήκαμεν), source of evils both private and public. Intergenerational transmission of sameness becomes discovery of war's origin.

Glaucon objects that Socrates makes men feast (ἑστιωμένους) and then calls the result a city of pigs (ὑῶν πόλιν), asking what else one would feed/fatten them with (ἐχόρταζες). ἑστιάω (of human feasting) and χορτάζω (of animal feeding) mark the contested boundary between human and animal dining.

Socrates redefines what they are examining (σκοποῦμεν, σκοποῦντες) from one city to two: the true city (ἀληθινὴ πόλις) and the inflamed city (φλεγμαίνουσαν πόλιν). The luxurious city's examination might let them see (κατίδοιμεν) where justice and injustice grow. The inquiry's scope expands with the city's expansion.

The territory sufficient (ἱκανή) to nourish the first city becomes insufficient (σμικρὰ δὴ ἐξ ἱκανῆς), requiring neighbors' land to be cut off (ἀποτμητέον) to have sufficient land (ἱκανὴν ἕξειν) for pasture and tillage. Sufficiency measured within becomes insufficiency requiring external seizure.

ὄψον, τραγήματα, κλῖναι, and τράπεζαι all move from absence or simplicity through Glaucon's objection into Socrates' expanded catalogues at 373a. Each word traces the movement from the simple city to the luxurious one.

Three dense catalogues accumulate at 373a-c: luxury goods (perfumes, incense, courtesans, gold, ivory), imitative and performative occupations (hunters, imitators, poets, rhapsodes, actors, dancers), and service occupations (tutors, wet-nurses, beauticians, barbers, cooks, butchers). The city's expansion generates proliferating lists.

new_signals.observation: πόλις recurs five times at 372e-373b as the inquiry shifts from examining one city to examining two (true, luxurious), and the luxurious city is declared in need of enlargement (μείζονά).

γίγνομαι and related forms (γένεσις, ἐμφύω) mark generation: how a city comes to be, how justice and injustice grow in cities (ἐμφύονται), and war's genesis (γένεσιν) as source of evils that come to be (γίγνεται).

elements.context: ταῖς πόλεσιν καὶ ἰδίᾳ καὶ δημοσίᾳ κακὰ γίγνεται

new_signals.observation: War's evils are specified as both private (ἰδίᾳ) and public (δημοσίᾳ), a paired adverbial construction marking the scope of harm.
Glaucon says those reclining on couches are those intending not to suffer hardship (μὴ ταλαιπωρεῖσθαι). Luxury is defined negatively as the absence of labor or suffering.

μόνον appears at both pivot points: when Socrates expands the inquiry beyond examining one city alone, and when he limits the conclusion to war's genesis alone without yet saying whether war works evil or good.
